items.name: Build Your Own Agent Stack
items.description: The complete build for a self-hosted AI agent system that runs your business 24/7 — on hardware you already own, for $0/month in API costs. This is the guide to the system in the screenshots: 41 specialised agents running 377 scheduled jobs across 10 free providers, on one Mac. Not a theory of how you might build one. 14 pages, six sections: What it does right now — the actual jobs the system performs daily, so you know what you are building toward. The $0/month architecture — the core concept, the stack layer by layer, the free providers, the routing logic that picks a model per task, and the exact .env to create. Agent structure — all 41 agents — the full directory with each agent's role, the IDENTITY.md system that defines them, and how memory and skills attach. The cron system — the commands you will actually use, and how jobs are grouped so they do not all fire at once. The bridge architecture — how the pieces talk, and the key files to know. Getting started checklist — install, keys, Chrome bridge, then editing each identity for your own niche. What this is not: a hosted product, a course, or a one-click installer. You will be editing config files and reading logs. If that sounds like work rather than a hobby, this is the wrong purchase. On the numbers: the agent and job counts in this guide are generated from the running system each time it is built, not typed in. If you see 41 agents on this page, the guide says 41 too.

items.name: Autonomous Agent Blueprints — 5 Real Workflows from a Working AI Business System
items.description: What if I showed you exactly how my AI system works — not theory, not a course, the actual scripts? This is 5 technical blueprints pulled straight from the OpenClaw system running my business right now. Every blueprint documents a real workflow: what it does, what you need, how to set it up, the exact commands to run, and what to expect. **What's inside:** **01 — The 5-Platform Content Pipeline** One Python script. One topic. Five platforms simultaneously — TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, Twitter, Facebook. AI generates the concept, writes the script, produces the video, and posts everything in a single command. 3–8 minutes start to finish. **02 — The AI Creative Director** A script that researches 14 top creators in your niche before any content gets made. Pulls live signals from Hacker News and Reddit. Produces a specific brief: exact opening line, angle, visual direction, what to avoid. Runs automatically before every post. **03 — The Zero-Cost Social Posting System** Direct API posting to TikTok and Instagram — no browser, no Selenium, no manual login. Two-step upload: presign → S3 → post. Returns a live URL. Used by the full pipeline automatically. **04 — The Free AI Voice Generator** Professional-quality voiceover for every video, free, no API key. The Kokoro tts.ai engine generates broadcast-quality narration, polls for completion, converts to MP3 via ffmpeg. Plugs into the video pipeline automatically. **05 — The Autonomous Agent Schedule** The scheduling layer that makes everything run without you. 88 cron jobs, 18 specialized agents, failure alerts to Telegram. Full setup guide — starter 5-cron schedule included, copy-paste commands ready. --- **Each blueprint includes:** - What it is (plain English) - Exact requirements (no surprise dependencies) - Step-by-step setup - Copy-paste commands - Expected output (what success looks like) - Troubleshooting table --- **This is for you if:** - You've done some AI automation and want to see how a full system fits together - You're building a content or lead-gen operation and want real infrastructure, not tutorial demos - You want to run agents on a schedule without a SaaS subscription **This is not:** - A beginner intro to AI - A video course - Theoretical advice about automation --- **Requirements:** - Python 3.9+ - macOS (scripts use macOS tools; adaptable to Linux) - At least one free AI API key (Groq, Gemini, Mistral, or Cerebras — all have free tiers) - ffmpeg (free, one install command) --- Questions? Email printedrevolution@gmail.com or find me at @therealmacsteel. ---

items.name: AI Search Readiness Audit
items.description: Find out whether AI assistants can find, understand, and recommend your business — scored 0-100, with the evidence attached. When a buyer asks ChatGPT, Claude, or Perplexity for a business like yours, 3 things decide whether you appear: whether AI crawlers can read your site, whether the engines know who you are, and whether you get named in your own category. This audit measures all 3 against your live domain and ranks what to fix first. What you get A report scored 0-100 across 3 weighted legs, emailed to you: Technical readiness — 50% of the score. 8 scored checks, 100 points: AI crawler access in robots.txt (30 pts, tested per bot for GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and Google-Extended), sitemap.xml validity and URL count (15 pts), JSON-LD schema types (15 pts), llms.txt (10 pts), title tag (10 pts), meta description (10 pts), H1 structure (5 pts), homepage weight (5 pts). Every check prints its points and the raw value behind it. Entity recognition — 25%. We query live AI models about your business by name and domain, then score how accurate and complete the answers are. The actual answers are quoted in the report. Citation presence — 25%. We ask the category questions your buyers ask, and record whether you were named, ranked, or absent. Prioritized fixes. Each gap becomes a specific fix ordered by impact — not "improve your SEO" but "ClaudeBot is blocked at line 4 of your robots.txt, so 3 of the 4 major assistants cannot read your site at all." Two real results, not mockups A live run on 2026-08-03 scored a restaurant site 70.0/100 on technical readiness, 16.7/100 on entity recognition, and 40.0/100 on citations — 49.2/100 overall, "PARTIALLY READY". All 4 AI crawlers were allowed and robots.txt was clean, yet the site still landed under 50, because the engines could not reliably say what the business was or name it in its category. The half you can check yourself was fine; the other half was the problem. A second run the same day scored anthropic.com 75.0/100 on technical readiness: 30/30 on crawler access, 15/15 on a sitemap carrying 508 URLs, 10/10 on a 126-character meta description, 5/5 on a 176 KB homepage — but 0/15 on JSON-LD schema and 0/10 on llms.txt. Even a well-built site leaves 25 points of machine-readability on the table. How it works Enter your domain at checkout. That 1 field is the only input we need, and we never guess it — if it is missing or unclear, we email you before running anything. Turnaround Within 72 hours — a deadline, not a hope. Most audits finish in under 5 minutes; the 72-hour window exists so a provider outage or a site that is briefly down never becomes a missed promise. What this is not Not a consulting call, not an implementation service, not a ranking promise. We do not edit your site and we do not submit you anywhere. This is a measurement of where you stand on 3 axes and what to fix first. Honest degradation: if a leg cannot be assessed — your site is unreachable, a model provider is down, or your robots.txt blocks our fetch too — the report marks that leg "not assessable" and reweights the remaining legs. In the sample above, an earlier run of anthropic.com scored 75.0/100 on 1 assessed leg and said so on its face rather than inventing the other 2. We never fill gaps with filler. Refund If we cannot complete your audit, you get a refund instead of a padded report. Reply to the delivery email — it reaches a real person, usually the same day.

items.name: Agent Prompt Pack
items.description: Twenty-five prompts for building autonomous AI agents — each one carrying the moment to use it, what good output looks like, the way it goes wrong, and the fix. Most prompt packs hand you text and wish you luck. The prompt is the easy part. What's missing is the context: when to reach for it, how to tell whether the answer is any good, and the specific way the obvious version fails. That context is the whole product here — it's why this is 6,200 words for 25 prompts instead of 2,700. Every prompt ships with four things: When — the moment you reach for it Expected output — what good looks like, so you can tell it worked Failure mode — the specific way the naive version goes wrong Tip — the non-obvious thing that makes it land The failure modes are real, not hypothetical. They come from running a 42-agent system with 368 scheduled jobs on one Mac at $0/month in API costs. A sample of what's in there: A health check that read a config field and reported healthy while the browser held zero session cookies and could not load a single authenticated page. It was reading a record of intent and reporting it as fact. except Exception that did not catch the exception — a safety gate called sys.exit(), and SystemExit inherits from BaseException. The guard meant to make failure safe was killing the caller instead. A maintenance script whose every health branch was silently "command not found", so it declared "browser down — restarting" on every run while the browser was fine. A write that passed the lock, the file hash and the journal and was still wrong, because all three watch bytes and staleness is semantic. Also inside: an architecture diagram of the loop every agent lives in, a table mapping each layer to its prompts and its most common failure, a worked example showing a real input with its real output (and what a failing output looks like, so you can recognise one), and 15 links to genuinely free tools and docs — every URL fetched and confirmed working before publication. What this is not: a course, a framework, or a codebase. There is nothing to install. If you want copy-paste code that runs an agent today, this is the wrong purchase — this is design-level material. And if you have already shipped several agents to production, you will likely know a third of these failure modes already. Costs nothing to run. Every prompt works against a local model (Ollama) or a free cloud tier. No paid API key at any point. Try before you pay: the 7-prompt starter set from the same system is free — search "7 Prompts From a Live Autonomous Agent Stack". If that one earns its keep, this is the full set. 25 prompts · 100 annotations · ~6,200 words · markdown · yours forever, updates included.

items.name: 7 Prompts From a Live Agent Stack
items.description: Seven prompts. That is the whole product. Not a 200-prompt dump you will never read — seven that are load-bearing in a system currently running 42 agents and 367 scheduled jobs on one M1 MacBook, at $0/month in API costs. What each one does: 1 · Agent Identity Brief — the template that defines every agent in the stack. Role, exact output format, and one hard constraint. This is the difference between an agent that behaves the same way on job 400 as it did on job 1, and one that drifts. 2 · Cron Task Specification — how to describe a scheduled job so it runs unattended without you babysitting it. 3 · Build-in-Public Content — turning real system events into posts, without inventing progress you did not make. 4 · Lead Scoring (Local Model) — written specifically for a small local model, so it costs nothing to run at volume. 5 · Self-Heal Diagnostic — what you hand a model when something broke and you need the cause, not sympathy. 6 · Free Model Routing — deciding which model gets which job when your budget for models is zero. 7 · Daily Status Report — the one that stops a system from reporting that everything is fine while it quietly is not. How to run them: replace the [BRACKETED] fields, then run against local Ollama or any free cloud tier. Nothing here needs a paid API key. Honest about the size: seven prompts, roughly 1,600 words. If you want volume, this is the wrong purchase. What you are buying is that each one has already survived contact with a system that runs unattended — a vague version of prompt 1 produced a vague agent, and the blunt version in here did not. 7 prompts · markdown · yours forever, updates included.
